calibracao: O vídeo mostra o réu dando o soco, mas não mostra os segundos anteriores, quando a defesa alega que a vítima o empurrou primeiro.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 31, a retail store manager, is charged with assault after a fight outside a sports bar at about 11:40 p.m. The complainant suffered a broken nose and needed six stitches above the left eye.

A security camera above the bar entrance shows {NAME} striking the complainant twice in the face. The camera does not cover the two or three seconds before the first punch, because both people stepped partly out of frame. The bouncer testified that the two had argued inside over a spilled drink and that {NAME} "looked angry" on the way out. The complainant testified to being punched without warning while walking to a car.

{NAME} testified that the complainant followed {him} outside, shouted threats, and shoved {him} hard against a parked car, and that {he} punched only to get free. A bartender confirmed that the complainant left the bar right after {NAME}, but did not see what happened outside. Responding officers noted a scrape on {NAME}'s elbow. The complainant's blood alcohol level was 0.14; {NAME}'s was 0.06.

The prosecution argues that two punches to the face, including one after the complainant had stepped back, go beyond what self-defense allows. The defense argues that the video starts too late to show who began the fight.

calibracao: A identificação depende de uma única testemunha, a vários metros e à noite, que reconheceu o réu numa sequência de fotos dias depois; há um álibi parcial por mensagens de celular.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 26, a bank loan officer, is charged with assault for a beating at a bus stop at around 10:15 p.m. The complainant suffered a fractured wrist and bruised ribs and could not describe the attacker, who wore a dark jacket with the hood up.

A food truck worker about 15 meters away watched the attack under a streetlight. Four days later, the worker picked {NAME} out of a six-photo lineup and told the detective, "I'm pretty sure, maybe 80 percent." The attacker took the complainant's phone, and that phone connected to a cell tower near {NAME}'s apartment about 40 minutes after the attack. Police found no stolen property and no dark jacket during a search of the apartment.

{NAME} testified that {he} was at home all evening. Phone records show {him} sending text messages from home at 9:58 p.m. and 10:31 p.m.; the bus stop is about a 12-minute drive away. {His} roommate testified that {NAME} was home but admitted to falling asleep at around 10:00 p.m.

The prosecution argues that the eyewitness identification and the phone's location point to the defendant. The defense argues that the identification is uncertain and that the tower covers several thousand residents.

calibracao: A lesão é grave e o réu admite a agressão, mas alega legítima defesa contra um ataque com garrafa; a garrafa nunca foi encontrada.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 38, a city bus driver, is charged with assault after a confrontation in a convenience store parking lot. The complainant suffered a concussion and a cut on the scalp that required staples.

{NAME} admits pushing the complainant, who fell and hit the curb. {He} testified that the two had a short argument about a parking space, and that the complainant then grabbed a glass bottle from a trash bin and swung it at {his} head. {NAME} said {he} pushed the complainant away to avoid being hit.

No bottle was recovered. The store clerk saw the push through the window but did not see the moments before it. The clerk testified that the complainant "had something in one hand" but could not say what it was. The complainant denied picking up anything and said {NAME} came at them "out of nowhere." Officers found broken glass in the lot, but the store manager testified that broken glass was common there.

{NAME} called 911 right after the fall and stayed at the scene until police arrived. The complainant has one prior conviction for disorderly conduct.

The prosecution argues that the push was disproportionate and that the bottle story was invented. The defense argues that the defendant reacted to a weapon and immediately sought help.

calibracao: Duas testemunhas dão versões opostas, ambas com vínculo com uma das partes; o laudo médico é compatível com as duas versões.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 29, a line cook, is charged with assault after a fight in the kitchen of the restaurant where {he} worked. The complainant, a coworker, suffered a deep bruise on the forearm and a sprained shoulder.

The complainant testified that {NAME} became angry over an order mix-up and struck them with a metal ladle. A dishwasher, who is a close friend of the complainant, supported that version. A second cook, who carpools with {NAME}, testified that the complainant grabbed {NAME}'s collar first and that {NAME} raised the ladle only to block.

The emergency physician testified that the forearm bruise could come either from a blow or from a defensive block against a held object. The kitchen camera was broken that week. The restaurant manager testified that both employees had received written warnings for arguments during shifts in the previous month.

Text messages show that {NAME} wrote to a friend that night: "I lost it at work, I messed up." {NAME} testified that the message referred to yelling during the argument, not to hitting anyone.

The prosecution argues that the injuries and the defendant's own message show an intentional attack. The defense argues that the evidence is balanced and that the defendant acted defensively.

calibracao: O DNA sob as unhas da vítima é do réu, mas o réu explica que houve contato físico numa briga anterior, mútua, no mesmo dia.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 34, an insurance claims adjuster, is charged with assault after a neighbor was found injured in the shared driveway of a duplex at about 7:00 p.m. The complainant suffered a fractured cheekbone and could not identify the attacker, saying they were struck from behind.

Material under the complainant's fingernails contained {NAME}'s DNA. The two had a long-running dispute about parking, and a third neighbor recorded a phone video at about 1:00 p.m. that day showing the two pushing and grabbing each other for about ten seconds before separating. No one was injured in that first incident.

{NAME} testified that {he} left for a client inspection at 3:00 p.m. and returned after 8:00 p.m. The client confirmed that {NAME} was at the inspection site until about 6:15 p.m. The drive back takes about 35 minutes. No one saw {NAME} between 6:15 p.m. and 8:00 p.m. A wooden board with traces of the complainant's blood was found by the driveway, but no usable fingerprints were found on it.

The prosecution argues that the DNA, the motive, and the window of opportunity point to the defendant. The defense argues that the DNA is explained by the recorded midday scuffle and that nothing places the defendant at the scene at 7:00 p.m.

calibracao: O réu admite ter dado um soco, mas diz que foi para defender um amigo; o amigo e a vítima contam versões diferentes sobre quem ameaçava quem.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 27, a hotel front desk clerk, is charged with assault after punching a stranger at a late-night food stand. The complainant lost a tooth and suffered a cut lip.

{NAME} admits throwing one punch. {He} testified that the complainant was standing very close to {his} friend, yelling, and had pulled back a fist, and that {he} struck first to stop what {he} believed was an imminent attack on the friend. The friend testified to the same account.

The complainant testified to complaining about the friend cutting in line, and said there was no raised fist and no threat. The vendor at the stand testified that the complainant was "loud and in the friend's face" but could not see the complainant's hands because of the counter. A phone video taken by a customer begins just after the punch and shows the complainant on the ground and {NAME} stepping back with open hands.

{NAME} has no criminal record. The complainant has a pending charge for threatening a parking attendant.

The prosecution argues that the defendant attacked someone who was only arguing and that defending another person requires a real threat. The defense argues that the defendant reasonably believed the friend was about to be hit.

calibracao: A vítima reconhece o réu com segurança, mas os dois tinham um conflito anterior, o que dá motivo para uma falsa acusação; não há outras provas diretas.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 42, a real estate agent, is charged with assault after a former business partner was attacked in a parking garage. The complainant suffered a broken arm.

The complainant testified to recognizing {NAME} clearly in the garage lights, from about two meters away, and to being hit with a metal pipe. The two had run a small property management business together until it closed eight months earlier, and the complainant was suing {NAME} over unpaid debts. The garage cameras were not recording that night due to a power issue.

A parking attendant saw a person in a gray rain jacket leave the garage on foot right after the attack but did not see the face. {NAME} owns a gray rain jacket, a very common item. No pipe was recovered.

{NAME} testified that {he} was at home alone watching television and denies any involvement. {His} phone shows no activity between 8:00 p.m. and 10:30 p.m.; the attack happened at 9:20 p.m. {NAME}'s home is about 20 minutes from the garage.

The prosecution argues that the complainant knows the defendant well and could not be mistaken. The defense argues that the complainant has a financial motive to blame the defendant and that nothing else ties {him} to the garage.

calibracao: As lesões confirmam a agressão e o réu estava no local, mas a vítima estava muito embriagada e mudou detalhes da versão entre o boletim e o julgamento.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 24, a college student who works part-time at a grocery store, is charged with assault after a house party. The complainant was found in the backyard with bruises on the face and a cracked rib.

At the hospital, the complainant told officers that "the person in the green shirt" pushed them down the back steps and kicked them. {NAME} was wearing a green shirt that night. At least two other guests also wore green, according to party photos. At trial, the complainant said {NAME} punched them before the fall, a detail not in the first statement. The complainant's blood alcohol level was 0.19.

Another guest testified to seeing {NAME} and the complainant arguing on the porch about ten minutes earlier. {NAME} admits the argument, about a borrowed speaker, but says {he} went back inside and left the party soon after. A ride-share receipt shows {NAME} was picked up 25 minutes before a guest called 911. No one saw the fall.

The prosecution argues that the defendant had a motive, matched the description, and argued with the complainant shortly before the attack. The defense argues that the description fits several guests and that the complainant's account is unreliable.

calibracao: Há confissão parcial do réu em depoimento policial, mas o réu alega que estava sob efeito de medicação e sem advogado, e a confissão contradiz um detalhe físico do caso.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 36, a hospital lab technician, is charged with assault after a stranger was beaten on a jogging trail early in the morning. The complainant suffered a fractured jaw and described the attacker only as a person in a gray sweatshirt.

{NAME} was stopped near the trail about an hour later, wearing a gray sweatshirt. In a recorded police interview that lasted four hours, {NAME} eventually said, "Fine, maybe I hit someone, I don't remember." Medical records show {he} had taken a prescribed sedative the night before. {He} did not have a lawyer during the interview, although {he} had waived that right in writing.

In the interview, {NAME} said the fight happened "by the bridge," but the attack took place about 800 meters from the bridge. No blood was found on {his} clothes or hands. A trail camera captured a person in a gray sweatshirt running away, but the image is too blurry to show the face.

{NAME} testified that {he} walks the trail daily after night shifts and only agreed with the detectives so the interview would end.

The prosecution argues that the defendant's admission, clothing, and presence near the trail prove guilt. The defense argues that the admission is unreliable and contradicts the known facts.

calibracao: O réu ficou sobre a vítima no chão e a câmera mostra golpes, mas a defesa alega que o réu imobilizava a vítima até a chegada da polícia depois de uma tentativa de roubo; a vítima nega ter tentado roubar.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 45, a property manager, is charged with assault after a confrontation near an ATM. The complainant suffered two broken ribs and facial bruises.

{NAME} testified that the complainant approached {him} at the ATM, demanded money, and grabbed {his} wallet, and that {he} wrestled the complainant to the ground and held them there while shouting for someone to call the police. The complainant denies demanding anything and testified to asking {NAME} only for directions.

A bank camera shows the two struggling. The footage shows {NAME} on top of the complainant, delivering at least three blows while the complainant appears to be covering their head. The camera has no audio. {NAME}'s wallet was found on the ground about a meter away. A passerby who called 911 testified to hearing someone yell "give it back" but could not say who yelled it.

The complainant has a prior conviction for theft from three years ago. {NAME} has no criminal record and called the bank's emergency line from the scene.

The prosecution argues that, even if there was a robbery attempt, striking a person who was already on the ground and covering up was excessive. The defense argues that the defendant used force only until the threat ended.

calibracao: O réu saiu com itens não pagos do caixa de autoatendimento, mas o sistema registra falhas de leitura frequentes; a intenção é o ponto incerto.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 33, an insurance agent, is charged with retail theft after leaving a home improvement store with merchandise worth $612 that had not been paid for.

{NAME} used a self-checkout station to buy 14 items. The receipt shows payment for 11 items totaling $96. The three unpaid items were a cordless drill, a battery pack, and a set of drill bits, which were the most expensive items in the cart. A loss prevention officer watched the transaction on camera and stopped {NAME} past the exit doors.

The store's own maintenance log shows that this self-checkout station had 23 recorded scanning errors in the previous month, including items that beeped but did not register. The video shows {NAME} passing the drill over the scanner, but the screen is not visible in the recording. The officer testified that {NAME} "did not look at the screen once" and moved quickly.

When stopped, {NAME} immediately offered to pay and showed a banking app with enough funds. {He} has no criminal record. The prosecution notes that the three missed items were the three most expensive ones, which it argues is unlikely to be chance.

The prosecution argues that the pattern of missed items shows intent. The defense argues that the machine was known to be faulty and that the defendant's reaction shows an honest mistake.

calibracao: A identificação vem de imagens de baixa resolução e de um cartão de fidelidade usado no mesmo dia; o réu diz que emprestava o cartão.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 28, a bartender, is charged with retail theft for taking two pairs of wireless headphones worth $698 from an electronics store.

Security video shows a person in a gray baseball cap and dark jacket placing the headphones inside a backpack and leaving without paying at 4:12 p.m. The video is low resolution, and the face is partly hidden by the cap. Twenty minutes earlier, the same person bought a phone charger at the register and scanned a loyalty card registered to {NAME}. The cashier could not describe the customer.

Police showed the video to {NAME}'s former coworker, who said the person "could be" {NAME} because of the way they walk. No headphones were found during a search of {NAME}'s apartment. {NAME} owns a gray baseball cap.

{NAME} testified that {he} often lets friends use {his} loyalty card number for discounts and that {he} was at work at the time. The bar's timekeeping system shows {him} clocking in at 4:45 p.m.; the bar is about 25 minutes from the store. No coworker could confirm when {NAME} actually arrived.

The prosecution argues that the loyalty card, the matching cap, and the coworker's statement identify the defendant. The defense argues that none of this evidence shows the face and that the card was shared.

calibracao: O valor é o ponto disputado: o preço de etiqueta passa de US$ 500, mas o preço promocional do dia ficava abaixo, o que mudaria a tipificação.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 40, a high school teacher, is charged with retail theft of merchandise worth over $500 from a department store.

A store detective saw {NAME} remove the security tags from two winter coats in a fitting room and leave the store wearing one coat and carrying the other in a shopping bag. {NAME} was stopped outside with both coats. The ticket price on each coat was $265, for a total of $530.

The store was holding a sale that weekend, and signs on the coat rack advertised "30% off all outerwear." At the sale price, the total would have been $371. The store manager testified that the company always values stolen goods at the ticket price. The prosecution relies on that ticket value.

{NAME} does not deny leaving with the coats. {He} testified that {he} meant to pay at a register on another floor and forgot because {he} was on a phone call. The fitting room attendant testified that {NAME} spent about 15 minutes in the fitting room and seemed calm. The removed tags were found in a fitting room trash can. {NAME} had $40 in cash and two credit cards with available credit.

The prosecution argues that removing security tags shows intent and that the ticket value applies. The defense argues that intent was not proven and that the merchandise was worth less than $500 on that day.

calibracao: A mercadoria estava na sacola do réu, mas um acompanhante pode tê-la colocado ali; o acompanhante tem antecedentes e não depôs.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 23, a part-time grocery store clerk, is charged with retail theft of vitamins and electric toothbrushes worth $544 from a drugstore.

{NAME} entered the store with an acquaintance. A camera shows the two walking together through the health products aisle, where the acquaintance's back blocks the view of the shelves for about 40 seconds. After the alarm sounded at the exit, a store employee found the merchandise in a tote bag carried by {NAME}. The acquaintance ran away and was never charged.

{NAME} testified that {he} did not know the items were in {his} bag and that the acquaintance had asked to "put something" in it while {he} was looking at {his} phone. The tote bag was open at the top. The employee testified that {NAME} looked "surprised" when the alarm went off but then said, "Please don't call the police."

The acquaintance has two prior shoplifting convictions and could not be found to testify. {NAME} has a prior juvenile record for vandalism that the jury was told about only to judge credibility.

The prosecution argues that the goods were in the defendant's bag and that the defendant asked the employee not to call the police. The defense argues that the acquaintance planted the items and that the defendant's reaction was fear, not guilt.

calibracao: Os itens furtados foram anunciados à venda numa conta ligada ao e-mail do réu, mas a conta foi acessada de mais de um aparelho e o réu diz que foi invadida.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 35, a real estate agent, is charged with retail theft for taking four smart home cameras worth $760 from a big-box store.

Store video shows a person in a gray rain jacket and sunglasses taking the cameras from a shelf and leaving through the garden center exit without paying. The face is not clearly visible. Two days later, four cameras of the same model, still sealed, were listed for sale on an online marketplace. The listing account was created with {NAME}'s email address, and the listing photos were taken on a kitchen counter that matches the one in {NAME}'s apartment.

Records from the marketplace show the account was accessed from two different phones, one of which belongs to {NAME}. The other phone was never identified. {NAME} testified that {his} email account had been hacked months earlier and that {he} had reported the hack to the email provider; the provider's records confirm a report but cannot confirm the hack. {NAME} admits owning a gray rain jacket.

{NAME} has sublet a room in the apartment to short-term guests several times in the past year. No cameras were found in the apartment.

The prosecution argues that the listing, the kitchen counter, and the jacket point to the defendant. The defense argues that other people had access to the apartment and the account.

calibracao: O réu passou pelo caixa com o carrinho e pagou parte das compras; um televisor ficou na parte de baixo do carrinho. Esquecimento ou ocultação?
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 46, a postal carrier, is charged with retail theft for leaving a warehouse club with a television worth $649 that had not been paid for.

{NAME} went through a staffed checkout with a full cart. The cashier scanned 31 items worth $287, but the television, in a large box on the lower rack of the cart, was not scanned. At the exit, the receipt checker noticed the box and stopped {NAME}.

The cashier testified to not seeing the box and to having asked, as usual, "anything on the bottom?" The cashier could not remember what {NAME} answered. The checkout video has no audio. The video shows that a bulky pack of paper towels was placed on top of the cart's lower rack, partly covering the box.

{NAME} testified that {he} did not hear the question in the noisy checkout area and believed the cashier had scanned everything. {He} paid with a membership card in {his} own name and offered to pay for the television right away. The store has a policy of prosecuting all unpaid items over $500.

The prosecution argues that placing paper towels over the box was an attempt to hide it and that the defendant ignored the cashier's question. The defense argues that it was an honest mistake by a customer who was paying with a card in {his} own name.

calibracao: O fiscal viu os vinhos irem para a bolsa, mas perdeu o réu de vista por um minuto; as garrafas apareceram do lado de fora de uma porta lateral, e o vídeo não mostra quem abriu essa porta.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 30, a pharmacist, is charged with retail theft for taking three bottles of premium wine worth $540 from a supermarket.

A loss prevention officer testified to watching {NAME} put the three bottles into a large shoulder bag in the wine aisle. The officer followed {NAME} but lost sight of {him} for about one minute when {NAME} turned into a hallway leading to the restrooms and to a side door to the parking lot. {NAME} then walked out through the main exit without paying for anything. The officer stopped {him} in the parking lot and searched the bag, which contained no wine. Thirty minutes later, staff found the three bottles behind a planter just outside the side door.

The wine aisle camera was not working that day. The hallway camera shows {NAME} entering and leaving the hallway; it also shows the side door opening once during that minute, but a stack of boxes blocks the view of who opened it. Fingerprints on the bottles were smudged and could not be compared.

{NAME} testified that {he} changed {his} mind about buying the wine and left the bottles on a shelf in the hallway, and that someone else must have carried them outside. The officer testified that there was no shelf in the hallway.

The prosecution argues that the defendant carried the bottles out through the side door to collect them later. The defense argues that no one saw the defendant leave the store with any merchandise.

calibracao: Trocas fraudulentas com recibo de outro cliente; o réu fez as devoluções, mas alega que agia a pedido de um conhecido que lhe deu os produtos e o recibo.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 27, a call center representative, is charged with retail theft for a return scheme at a sporting goods store. Prosecutors say {NAME} took two pairs of hiking boots from the shelves, then "returned" them at the service desk using an old receipt, receiving $520 in store credit.

Video shows {NAME} entering the store with an empty shopping bag, walking to the footwear section, and then going to the service desk with two boxes of boots about ten minutes later. The receipt {NAME} used was from a purchase made three weeks earlier with a credit card that does not belong to {him}. The cardholder could not be identified.

{NAME} testified that an acquaintance asked {him} to return the boots, gave {him} the receipt and the bag of boots in the parking lot, and promised to split the credit. {He} said {he} walked to the footwear section only to compare prices. The footwear section camera shows {NAME} near the boot shelves but does not show {him} removing boxes. Phone records show several calls between {NAME} and an unregistered number that morning.

The prosecution argues that the defendant took the boots from the shelf and returned them for credit. The defense argues that the defendant was used by someone else and did not know the boots were stolen.

calibracao: Prova forte de que alguém com o crachá do réu levou eletrônicos do depósito, mas o crachá foi relatado como perdido dois dias antes, e o relato foi tardio.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 37, an assistant store manager, is charged with retail theft for removing two laptops worth $1,480 from the stockroom of the electronics store where {he} worked.

The store's access system shows that {NAME}'s badge opened the stockroom at 9:52 p.m., after closing. Inventory counted the next morning was short two laptops. The stockroom camera was pointed at the loading dock and did not show the shelves. The rear door alarm was turned off with the manager code, which is known to four employees, including {NAME}.

{NAME} testified that {he} lost {his} badge two days before and reported it to the store manager. The store manager confirms a report, but says it was made by text message the morning after the theft, not two days before. {NAME} says {he} told the manager in person earlier and texted later to make it official. {NAME}'s phone was at {his} home, about 15 minutes away, at 9:52 p.m., but the prosecution notes that a phone can be left at home.

No laptops were found. {NAME} has worked at the store for five years and had positive performance reviews.

The prosecution argues that the badge, the alarm code, and the late report point to the defendant. The defense argues that a lost badge explains the entry and that several people knew the code.

calibracao: Testemunha ocular confiável (funcionário) e itens recuperados perto do réu, mas o réu estava num grupo de quatro pessoas e a testemunha descreveu roupas comuns.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 22, a university student, is charged with retail theft of sunglasses worth $585 from a boutique in a shopping mall.

A sales associate testified to seeing a customer in a green jacket slip four pairs of designer sunglasses into a coat pocket while the associate was helping another customer. The customer left with a group of four people. The associate alerted mall security, who found the group about five minutes later in the food court. {NAME} was the only person in the group wearing a green jacket. The four pairs of sunglasses were found in a trash can about ten meters from the table where the group was sitting.

The associate later identified {NAME} as the person in the green jacket, but admitted that two other customers in the store that afternoon also wore green. The boutique camera was not recording because of a system update. No sunglasses were found on any member of the group.

{NAME} testified that {he} was in the boutique only briefly and never touched the sunglasses. The other three members of the group testified that they did not see anyone take anything. The prosecution notes that they are close friends of {NAME}.

The prosecution argues that the associate's account, the green jacket, and the nearby trash can establish guilt. The defense argues that the identification relies only on clothing and that anyone in the food court could have discarded the sunglasses.

calibracao: Impressão digital do réu na janela arrombada, mas o réu tinha examinado aquela mesma janela numa vistoria de seguro cinco semanas antes.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 32, an insurance appraiser, is charged with residential burglary of a detached house. While the owners were away for a weekend, someone forced open a rear window and took jewelry, a laptop, and about $800 in cash.

Investigators lifted two fingerprints from the outside of the forced window frame. Both matched {NAME}. Fresh pry marks on the frame matched a flat screwdriver, a common tool. About five weeks earlier, {NAME} had inspected storm damage to the rear windows of the house for the owners' insurance company, as the claim file confirms.

The owners testified that they washed the outside of the windows "sometime in the past month" but could not say exactly when. A fingerprint expert testified that prints on a painted window frame can last for weeks if not cleaned, and that the age of a print cannot be determined.

{NAME} testified that {he} spent the weekend at home. {His} roommate confirmed that {NAME} was home Saturday evening, but was away Sunday afternoon, when the neighbors believe the burglary happened because a dog barked for a long time. None of the stolen items were found during a search of {NAME}'s apartment and car.

The prosecution argues that the prints were on the exact window that was forced. The defense argues that the prints are explained by the insurance inspection and that nothing else links the defendant to the burglary.

calibracao: O réu penhorou uma joia furtada na própria casa de penhores, com documento próprio, dois dias depois; diz que comprou a joia de um desconhecido.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 29, a restaurant shift manager, is charged with residential burglary of an apartment from which a gold watch, two rings, and a tablet were taken.

Two days after the burglary, {NAME} sold the gold watch to a pawn shop, showing {his} own driver's license and signing the receipt. The watch had a unique engraving that the owner described before it was recovered. The other items were never found.

{NAME} testified that {he} bought the watch for $150 from a stranger at a gas station, believing it was a good deal, and sold it to the pawn shop for $400 the same week. {He} could not give the stranger's name or a clear description. The gas station's cameras keep footage for only 24 hours.

There were no fingerprints, shoe prints, or DNA linking {NAME} to the apartment. {NAME}'s phone was not near the apartment on the day of the burglary, according to cell tower records. The watch's market value is about $1,200. A detective testified that buying a watch for far less than its value is "a classic sign" of knowing it was stolen, which would be a different crime than burglary.

The prosecution argues that possession of recently stolen property, with a weak explanation, supports the inference that the defendant committed the burglary. The defense argues that the evidence shows, at most, that the defendant bought stolen property, not that {he} entered the apartment.

calibracao: Pegada de calçado no local compatível com o tênis do réu, mas o modelo é muito vendido; o celular do réu esteve na região, onde também mora um amigo do réu.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 25, a junior accountant, is charged with residential burglary of a townhouse. Someone kicked in the back door on a weekday morning and took two laptops and a gaming console.

Investigators photographed a muddy shoe print on the kitchen floor. The print matches the sole pattern and size of a running shoe found in {NAME}'s closet. A shoe expert testified that the model is one of the best-selling running shoes in the country and that the print showed no unique wear marks that would tie it to a specific pair.

Cell tower data places {NAME}'s phone in the area of the townhouse between 9:00 and 11:30 a.m. {NAME}'s close friend lives about four blocks away, and the friend testified that {NAME} came over that morning to help move furniture and stayed "most of the morning," but could not say whether {NAME} left for any period.

A neighbor saw a person in a dark hooded jacket carrying a large bag near the townhouse at about 10:15 a.m. but could not describe the face. {NAME} owns a dark hooded jacket. None of the stolen items were found.

The prosecution argues that the shoe print, the phone location, and the jacket together point to the defendant. The defense argues that each piece of evidence is common and that the defendant had an innocent reason to be in the area.

calibracao: DNA do réu numa bituca de cigarro no quintal da casa, mas o réu morou na casa ao lado até três meses antes e frequentava o quintal.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 38, a sales representative, is charged with residential burglary of a house. Someone broke a glass panel in the back door and stole a coin collection worth about $9,000.

A cigarette butt found on the back patio, about two meters from the broken door, contained {NAME}'s DNA. {NAME} lived in the house next door until three months before the burglary and was friendly with the homeowners. The homeowners testified that {NAME} sometimes smoked on their patio during backyard gatherings, and that they could not remember when they last swept the patio.

The homeowners had shown the coin collection to several visitors over the years, including {NAME}. A neighbor's camera recorded a car similar to {NAME}'s, a common silver sedan, passing on the street 40 minutes before the estimated time of the burglary. The plate is not readable.

{NAME} testified that {he} was at {his} new apartment that evening. {He} has no witnesses. Bank records show that {NAME} had fallen behind on rent and had received a late notice the week before. No coins were found, and no coin dealer in the region reported buying the collection.

The prosecution argues that the DNA, the knowledge of the collection, the car, and the financial pressure point to the defendant. The defense argues that the DNA could be months old and that the car and motive are speculation.

calibracao: Entrada sem arrombamento, com chave; o réu é ex-colega de apartamento e não devolveu a cópia, mas outras pessoas também tinham chaves.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 27, a graphic designer, is charged with residential burglary of an apartment {he} used to share with the complainant. Three months after {NAME} moved out, someone entered the apartment while it was empty and took a camera, two lenses, and an envelope with $1,500 in cash.

There was no forced entry. {NAME} admits never returning {his} key. The complainant testified that two other people also had keys: a dog walker and a former partner of the complainant. Both testified that they did not enter the apartment that day and gave alibis that were partly confirmed.

The complainant testified that {NAME} knew where the cash envelope was kept, because the two used to share a household budget. A text message from {NAME} sent two weeks before the burglary says, "You still owe me for the last two months of utilities, and I'm going to get it one way or another." {NAME} testified that the message was about filing a small claims case.

{NAME} says {he} was at a coworking space that afternoon. The coworking space logs show {his} badge entering at 1:10 p.m. and no exit record, because exits are not logged. The apartment is a 20-minute walk from the coworking space. None of the stolen items were found.

The prosecution argues that the key, the knowledge of the cash, and the threatening message point to the defendant. The defense argues that others had keys and that the message referred to a lawful claim.

calibracao: O réu foi encontrado de madrugada dentro da garagem anexa (parte da residência), com luvas e lanterna, mas nada foi levado; a tese da defesa é de que procurava um gato perdido, e o ponto disputado é a intenção de furtar no momento da entrada.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 34, a hospital pharmacist who works night shifts, is charged with residential burglary after being found at about 3:30 a.m. inside the attached garage of a house two blocks from {his} own home. Under state law, an attached garage is part of the dwelling.

The homeowner heard noises, looked out, and saw a person with a flashlight open the side door of the garage and step inside. The homeowner called 911. Police arrived within six minutes and found {NAME} inside the garage, wearing gloves and holding a flashlight, standing next to a shelf with power tools. Nothing was missing.

{NAME} testified that {his} cat had escaped that evening and that {he} was searching nearby yards after getting home from work. {He} said {he} heard a noise inside the garage, found the side door unlocked, and stepped in to look for the cat. A neighbor confirmed seeing a "lost cat" post from {NAME} on a local community app at 1:50 a.m. The cat was found two days later, three streets away.

The homeowner testified that the side door was locked earlier that night. Police did not test the handle for prints. {NAME} wears gloves on the way home from work in cold weather; the temperature that night was 2°C.

The prosecution argues that the defendant entered the garage with the intent to steal the tools. The defense argues that the defendant entered only to look for a lost pet, without any intent to commit a theft.

calibracao: Rastreador GPS escondido num notebook furtado levou à casa do réu, onde o notebook estava; o réu diz que o recebeu de presente de um colega de casa que se mudou.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 26, a barista, is charged with residential burglary of a house from which a laptop, a tablet, and a set of headphones were stolen during the day.

The laptop had tracking software. Two days after the burglary, the owner located it at a house where {NAME} rents a room with three other tenants. Police found the laptop in a shared living room, plugged in, with the owner's account still logged in. The tablet and headphones were not found.

One of the other tenants had moved out the day after the burglary and could not be located. {NAME} testified that this tenant brought the laptop home and said it had been "bought cheap from a friend." The remaining two tenants testified that they had never seen the laptop before, but also said they rarely used the living room.

A neighbor of the burglarized house saw a person on a bicycle leave the house carrying a backpack. {NAME} owns a bicycle, as do the other tenants. Phone location data places {NAME} at work during most of the estimated burglary window, but there is a 50-minute gap during {his} lunch break; the house is about 10 minutes away by bicycle.

The prosecution argues that the defendant had the stolen laptop and the opportunity to commit the burglary during the lunch break. The defense argues that the laptop was in a shared space and was brought in by a tenant who then disappeared.

calibracao: Um vizinho reconhece o réu, carteiro da rota, indo para os fundos da casa pouco antes do furto; mas a janela de tempo do furto é de dez horas e o réu ficou só quatro minutos no endereço.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 31, a postal mail carrier, is charged with residential burglary of a house on {his} delivery route. Someone entered through an unlocked back door during the day and took a tablet, a laptop, and several pieces of jewelry.

A neighbor testified to seeing {NAME}, whom the neighbor recognized as the regular mail carrier, walking along the side of the house toward the backyard at about 2:00 p.m. Postal scan records show that {NAME} delivered a package to that house at 1:57 p.m. The package was left at the front door.

The homeowners left for work at 8:00 a.m. and returned at 6:30 p.m., so the burglary could have happened at any time during that period. A different neighbor saw a person in a gray sweatshirt in the backyard "sometime in the afternoon" but could not describe the face.

{NAME} testified that {he} walked toward the side gate only to check whether there was a safer place to leave the package, as {he} sometimes does, and then left it at the front door. {His} postal vehicle's GPS shows {him} at the next stop four minutes later. None of the stolen items were found in {his} vehicle or home.

The prosecution argues that the defendant was seen going toward the back of the house shortly before the items went missing. The defense argues that four minutes was not enough time and that the burglary window was ten hours long.

calibracao: Perícia identifica fibras e vidro compatíveis na roupa do réu, mas ambas as provas são de classe (não individualizadoras); o réu tem um álibi parcial de um amigo.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 36, a freelance photographer, is charged with residential burglary of a house where a glass patio door was smashed and electronics worth about $4,000 were taken.

Police stopped {NAME} about one kilometer from the house, 50 minutes after a neighbor reported the sound of breaking glass. A lab analysis found three tiny glass fragments on {NAME}'s jacket with the same refractive index as the patio door glass. A glass expert testified that this type of glass is used in millions of doors and windows and that the match shows only that the fragments could have come from the door. Blue fibers found on the broken door frame were consistent with {NAME}'s jacket, a mass-produced item.

{NAME} testified that {he} spent the evening at a friend's home helping repair a broken window, which explains the glass. The friend confirmed this and showed a receipt for window glass bought that afternoon, but the friend's broken window used a different type of glass, according to the expert.

No stolen items were found on {NAME} or in {his} car. {NAME} has a conviction for burglary from 11 years ago.

The prosecution argues that the glass and fiber evidence, together with the stop near the scene, identify the defendant. The defense argues that the forensic matches are generic and that the defendant has a credible reason for having glass on the jacket.

calibracao: O réu confessou a um informante preso na mesma cela, que ganhou benefícios por depor; há detalhes corretos na confissão, mas eles foram divulgados pela imprensa.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 41, an insurance broker, is charged with residential burglary of a house from which a safe containing about $20,000 in cash and documents was removed.

The main evidence is the testimony of a person who shared a jail cell with {NAME} for three days after {his} arrest on an unrelated traffic warrant. The informant testified that {NAME} described "taking a safe out of a house on the lake road" and said it took two people to carry it. In exchange for testifying, the informant received a reduced sentence on a fraud charge.

The details the informant reported, including the lake road and the size of the safe, had appeared in a local news article a week earlier. The informant has testified in two previous cases. {NAME} denies ever talking about the burglary.

Investigators also found that {NAME} paid off a $6,000 car loan in cash two weeks after the burglary. {NAME} testified that the money came from selling a boat, and produced a handwritten bill of sale; the buyer could not be located. No fingerprints or DNA were found at the house.

The prosecution argues that the confession and the sudden cash payment show guilt. The defense argues that the informant had strong reasons to lie and only repeated details from the news.

calibracao: As transferências saíram do login do réu, mas a senha ficava num bilhete no monitor e outros dois funcionários usavam o mesmo computador.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 39, a staff accountant, is charged with embezzlement from the furniture company where {he} worked. Over seven months, 14 payments totaling $48,300 were sent from the company's bank account to a vendor that does not exist. The vendor's bank account was opened online with a stolen identity.

All 14 payments were approved in the accounting system under {NAME}'s login. {NAME} was one of three people in the accounting office, and the office shared one computer for bank approvals. Two coworkers testified that {NAME}'s password was written on a sticky note attached to that computer's monitor, a practice the company's auditors had criticized.

Four of the payments were approved on days when {NAME} was working from home, according to the badge system; the company's remote access logs show {NAME}'s account connected from {his} home internet address on those days. The other two employees' accounts do not show remote access on those days.

{NAME} testified that {he} never approved those payments and that anyone in the office could have used {his} login. Investigators found no unusual deposits in {NAME}'s bank accounts. {He} had taken on a large personal loan the year before.

The prosecution argues that the login records and remote access link the defendant to the payments. The defense argues that the password was public in the office and that no money was traced to the defendant.

calibracao: O réu depositou cheques da empresa na própria conta, mas alega que eram reembolsos autorizados verbalmente por um sócio que morreu antes do julgamento.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 44, an office operations manager, is charged with embezzlement from a small architecture firm. Over two years, {NAME} deposited 22 company checks, totaling $36,750, into {his} personal bank account.

{NAME} admits making the deposits. {He} testified that one of the firm's two founding partners verbally authorized the checks as reimbursement for expenses {he} paid personally, including software licenses and client dinners, and as an informal bonus. That partner died of a heart attack eight months before the trial. The surviving partner testified to knowing nothing about any reimbursement agreement and said that the firm's written policy requires receipts for every reimbursement.

{NAME} produced receipts for about $9,400 in business expenses paid with {his} own card during the same period. The memo lines on several checks say "reimb." in {NAME}'s handwriting. Two of the checks bear the deceased partner's signature; the others were signed with a signature stamp that {NAME} was allowed to use for routine bills.

The firm's bookkeeper testified that the deceased partner "was informal about money" and sometimes gave cash bonuses without recording them.

The prosecution argues that the defendant used the signature stamp to pay {himself} far more than any documented expense. The defense argues that the payments were authorized by a partner who can no longer testify.

calibracao: Faltas de caixa ocorreram em 9 de 11 turnos do réu, mas também em 4 turnos em que o réu não trabalhava; o caixa é compartilhado.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 26, a shift supervisor at a gas station convenience store, is charged with embezzlement of about $6,200 in cash over three months.

The store's records show cash shortages on 13 shifts. {NAME} supervised 9 of those 13 shifts. Shortages also occurred on 4 shifts {he} did not work. On {NAME}'s shifts, two cashiers also had access to the registers, and the supervisor was the only person with the code to the safe where cash was dropped.

The store's camera above the safe shows {NAME} opening the safe 38 times during those shifts. The video shows {him} counting cash, but the camera angle does not show whether any cash was removed. After {NAME} was suspended, shortages stopped for six weeks, then occurred twice more.

A cashier testified to once seeing {NAME} put "a folded stack of bills" into a jacket pocket; {NAME} testified that it was {his} own tip money from a second job. {NAME} has no prior record. {His} bank records show regular cash deposits of $100 to $200 during the period, which {he} says come from weekend work as a wedding photographer's assistant; {he} produced two payment messages from the photographer.

The prosecution argues that the pattern of shortages and the access to the safe point to the defendant. The defense argues that others had access and that shortages continued after the suspension.

calibracao: O réu criou um "funcionário fantasma" na folha de pagamento; há prova documental forte, mas o réu diz que cumpria ordem do gerente, que também foi denunciado e fez acordo para depor contra o réu.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 35, an accounting systems analyst responsible for payroll processing, is charged with embezzlement from a regional trucking company. For 15 months, a person who never worked at the company received biweekly paychecks totaling $41,600. The paychecks were deposited into an account controlled by the company's operations manager.

{NAME} created the fake employee record in the payroll system and approved each pay run. {NAME} admits creating the record but testified that the operations manager told {him} the person was a remote dispatcher hired off the books and that {he} should "just put them in the system." Emails show the operations manager sending {NAME} the fake employee's name, address, and bank details.

The operations manager was also charged and agreed to testify against {NAME} in exchange for a reduced sentence. The manager testified that {NAME} came up with the scheme and received $500 in cash from each paycheck. No cash payments to {NAME} were traced. {NAME}'s bank account shows no unusual deposits, but {he} bought a used car with $7,000 in cash during the period; {he} testified that the money came from savings.

Company policy required payroll staff to verify any new employee with a signed hiring form. No form exists for the fake employee.

The prosecution argues that the defendant knowingly created and paid a fake employee and shared in the proceeds. The defense argues that the defendant followed a manager's instructions and that the manager is lying to reduce a sentence.

calibracao: Reembolsos de devoluções lançados no cartão do réu sem mercadoria devolvida; o réu admite alguns e diz que eram trocas legítimas para clientes que não tinham cartão.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 24, a customer service desk associate at a department store, is charged with embezzlement for processing refunds onto {his} own debit card. Over four months, 31 refunds totaling $5,860 were paid to a card in {NAME}'s name. No returned merchandise matches most of those refunds.

{NAME} admits that the refunds went to {his} card. {He} testified that, on busy days, some customers who paid in cash wanted their refunds immediately, and that {he} refunded those amounts to {his} own card and handed the customers cash from {his} wallet, because the store's cash refund process took too long. {He} said a former supervisor told {him} this was acceptable.

The former supervisor denies giving that permission. The store found returned merchandise logged for 6 of the 31 refunds. For the other 25, there is no record of returned items. Store video for three of those refunds shows no customer at the desk at the time.

{NAME} withdrew cash from ATMs on most of the days the refunds were processed, which the defense says is consistent with replacing the cash {he} gave to customers. {NAME} has been employed at the store for three years with no prior discipline.

The prosecution argues that refunds without customers and without merchandise show theft. The defense argues that the defendant used an informal, unauthorized but honest workaround.

calibracao: Mercadoria do estoque foi vendida online numa conta com o endereço do réu, mas o réu divide a casa com um colega que também trabalha na empresa e tem acesso ao estoque.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 31, an inventory analyst at an electronics distributor, is charged with embezzlement of company inventory. Over six months, 46 new graphics cards worth $27,000 disappeared from the warehouse, and inventory records were adjusted to hide the losses.

The inventory adjustments were made under {NAME}'s user account, which {NAME} admits is used only by {him}. An online seller account, shipping from {NAME}'s home address, sold 39 graphics cards of the same model during that period. The seller account was registered to {NAME}'s housemate, who works at the same warehouse as a forklift operator.

{NAME} testified that {he} made the adjustments because the physical counts were lower than the system counts, which was {his} job, and that {he} reported the losses to the warehouse manager. The manager confirms receiving two emails from {NAME} about "unexplained shortages," but says {NAME} described them as counting errors. The housemate invoked the right to remain silent and did not testify.

Payments from the seller account went to the housemate's bank account. {NAME}'s account shows a transfer of $2,000 from the housemate, which {NAME} says was rent.

The prosecution argues that the defendant hid the losses so the housemate could sell the stolen cards and shared in the profits. The defense argues that the defendant did {his} job and reported the shortages, and that the housemate acted alone.

calibracao: Prova contábil de que o réu fez compras pessoais com o cartão corporativo; o réu alega que eram despesas de clientes e que perdeu os recibos numa mudança. O valor e o padrão de gastos pesam contra.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 47, a regional sales director at a medical equipment company, is charged with embezzlement for using a corporate credit card for personal purchases. An internal audit found $23,900 in charges over one year that the company classified as personal: hotel stays on weekends, restaurant meals near {NAME}'s home, and electronics.

{NAME} testified that most of the charges were legitimate client entertainment and travel and that {he} lost a folder of receipts during a move. Company policy requires receipts within 30 days, but {NAME}'s former manager testified that the policy was "loosely enforced" for senior sales staff. Two clients testified that {NAME} took them to dinner several times near {his} home. Neither client could remember the exact dates.

The audit found that 11 of the weekend hotel stays were in a resort town where {NAME} owns no property and has no clients. {NAME} said {he} met potential clients there at a conference; the conference took place on only two of those weekends. The electronics, a laptop and two tablets, were not in the company's asset records.

The prosecution argues that the defendant knowingly used company money for personal expenses and hid it with vague reports. The defense argues that the spending was a gray area tolerated by the company and handled as a disciplinary matter for other employees.

calibracao: Doações de uma ONG foram desviadas para uma conta aberta com dados do réu; o réu diz que teve a identidade roubada e há indícios disso, mas o dinheiro pagou uma dívida do réu.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 30, an operations coordinator at a nonprofit food bank, is charged with embezzlement of $18,400 in donations. Online donations made through a campaign page that {NAME} managed were sent to a payment account opened in {NAME}'s name instead of the nonprofit's account.

{NAME} testified that {he} never opened the payment account and that {his} identity had been stolen. {He} had filed a police report about identity theft four months before the donations began, after someone opened a credit card in {his} name. The payment account was opened from an internet address that investigators traced to a public library.

However, $6,000 from the payment account was used to pay off {NAME}'s overdue car loan, and another $3,200 went to {NAME}'s landlord. {NAME} testified that {he} did not notice those payments, because {he} had set up automatic payments from several accounts and did not check them closely. The rest of the money was withdrawn in cash at ATMs in another city.

The food bank's director testified that {NAME} had full access to the campaign page settings and was the only staff member who changed them during the period.

The prosecution argues that the money paid the defendant's debts and that only the defendant could change the campaign settings. The defense argues that the defendant was a known identity theft victim and that most of the money went elsewhere.

calibracao: A planilha manipulada estava no computador do réu e há confissão por e-mail, mas o e-mail é ambíguo e foi escrito depois de uma reunião sob pressão com a diretoria.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 37, a treasury analyst at a community credit union, is charged with embezzlement of $52,000. Investigators found that, over two years, small amounts were moved from dormant member accounts into an internal suspense account and then transferred to an outside account belonging to a company registered under a false name.

A spreadsheet tracking the dormant accounts and the transfers was found on {NAME}'s work computer. The transfers were made with two different employee logins, {NAME}'s and that of a coworker who left the credit union a year earlier and could not be found.

After a three-hour meeting with the board and the credit union's lawyer, {NAME} wrote an email to the board: "I should have reported what was happening with the dormant accounts. I'm sorry for my part in this." {NAME} testified that {his} "part" was failing to report suspicious transfers {he} had noticed, not making them, and that the spreadsheet was {his} own effort to track the problem.

The outside company's bank account was opened with a phone number that once belonged to the former coworker. No money was traced to {NAME}.

The prosecution argues that the spreadsheet, the login records, and the email admission show guilt. The defense argues that the defendant was investigating, not committing, the scheme and that the former coworker is the likely culprit.

calibracao: O réu vendeu móveis usados da empresa e ficou com o dinheiro; diz que acreditava ter permissão por um costume antigo, confirmado por um colega, mas negado pela empresa.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 43, a facilities coordinator at a commercial property company, is charged with embezzlement for selling the company's surplus office furniture and keeping the money. Over 18 months, {NAME} sold surplus furniture from building renovations to a used furniture dealer 17 times, receiving a total of $14,700.

The dealer's records show {NAME}'s name and driver's license number on every sale. {NAME} admits the sales. {He} testified that a former facilities director told {him} years earlier that staff could "take care of the old furniture" and keep the proceeds as a perk, and that this had been the practice for a long time. A maintenance technician who worked at the company for 12 years testified that the previous coordinator also sold surplus furniture and kept the money.

The company's current director testified that no such policy exists and that the renovation contracts list the surplus furniture as company property. The former facilities director could not be located. {NAME} did not report the income on {his} tax returns. {He} never mentioned the sales to the current director, who joined the company two years ago.

The prosecution argues that the defendant knew the furniture belonged to the company and hid the sales. The defense argues that the defendant honestly believed the furniture could be kept, which would mean {he} did not knowingly take company property.

calibracao: O carro do réu tem dano compatível e estava no local, mas o réu divide o carro com um colega de casa; não se sabe quem dirigia.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 29, a pharmacy manager, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a cyclist at about 11:20 p.m. on a two-lane road. The cyclist suffered a broken leg. A witness wrote down a partial plate and described a silver hatchback.

Police found {NAME}'s silver hatchback the next morning with a cracked headlight and a dent on the front right fender. Paint transfer from the bicycle matched the dent. The plate matches the witness's partial plate.

{NAME} shares the car with {his} housemate, and both have keys. {NAME} testified that {he} was asleep at home that night and that the housemate had borrowed the car to visit friends. The housemate testified to returning the car at 9:30 p.m., before the collision, and to being at home after that. Neither person's phone shows movement after 10:00 p.m., but the prosecution notes that the driver may not have carried a phone.

The witness saw the driver only from behind and could not describe the person. No camera recorded the driver. The car's seat position fit both {NAME} and the housemate.

The prosecution argues that the defendant's car was involved and that the defendant, as the owner and primary user, was most likely the driver. The defense argues that two people had access to the car and that the prosecution cannot prove who was driving.

calibracao: O réu admite que dirigia e que sentiu um impacto, mas diz que achou que tinha passado num buraco; o pedestre foi atingido de raspão e caiu fora do campo de visão.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 52, a high school chemistry teacher, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a pedestrian at about 6:40 p.m. on a rainy winter evening. The pedestrian was walking in the road at the edge of a narrow street without sidewalks, was struck by a side mirror, and fell into a ditch, suffering a broken wrist and a concussion.

{NAME} admits driving on that street at the time and admits feeling "a bump." {He} testified that {he} thought {he} had hit a pothole, which is common on that street, and kept driving home. The next morning, {NAME} noticed that the right side mirror was broken and reported it to {his} insurer as pothole damage.

A neighbor who heard the impact testified that it was "a loud bang" and that the car did not slow down. The pedestrian was wearing dark clothing and no reflective gear. An accident reconstruction expert testified that a driver could have seen the pedestrian in the headlights for about two seconds before impact, but that after impact the pedestrian fell to the right, outside the driver's line of sight.

The street has several deep potholes, which the city had been asked to repair. {NAME} has a clean driving record.

The prosecution argues that a loud impact and a broken mirror should have made any reasonable driver stop and check. The defense argues that the defendant honestly believed {he} hit a pothole and did not know a person was involved.

calibracao: O réu comunicou o furto do próprio carro na manhã seguinte ao atropelamento; a acusação diz que foi uma comunicação falsa, mas o carro foi achado abandonado com a ignição forçada.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 34, a software tester, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a motorcyclist at an intersection at about 1:15 a.m. A traffic camera recorded a gray SUV running a red light, hitting the motorcycle, and driving away. The camera image shows the plate, which is registered to {NAME}, but not the driver.

At 7:40 a.m. the same morning, {NAME} reported the SUV stolen from the street outside {his} apartment. Police found the SUV two days later, abandoned in a parking lot about three kilometers from the collision, with front-end damage. The ignition had been forced with a tool, and the steering column was cracked.

A detective testified that thieves usually force ignitions, but also that owners who want to cover up a crime sometimes damage their own cars to fake a theft. A latent fingerprint on the driver's door handle matched {NAME}, which is expected for the owner. No other usable prints were found.

{NAME}'s phone was connected to {his} home internet from 11:00 p.m. to 7:30 a.m. {NAME} testified that {he} was asleep. The prosecution notes that {NAME} had a prior DUI conviction five years ago and suggests a motive to avoid another arrest.

The prosecution argues that the theft report was invented to cover up the collision. The defense argues that the forced ignition and the phone data are consistent with a real theft.

calibracao: Testemunha identifica o réu como motorista e o carro tem dano compatível, mas a testemunha só viu o rosto por um instante e no escuro, e o reconhecimento ocorreu numa audiência em que o réu era o único acusado presente.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 27, a restaurant host, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a pedestrian in a crosswalk at about 9:50 p.m. The pedestrian suffered a fractured hip.

A bus driver waiting at the light testified to seeing the driver's face through the side window for "a second or two" as the car turned and drove off. The street lighting was poor. Days later, the bus driver saw {NAME} in the courtroom during a preliminary hearing, where {NAME} was the only person charged, and said, "That's the driver." The bus driver was never shown a photo lineup.

{NAME}'s blue sedan has a dent in the front bumper. A paint expert testified that the dent is consistent with hitting a person but could also have come from a low-speed impact with a pole. {NAME} testified that {he} hit a parking pole a week before and had not fixed it; {he} has no record of reporting that damage.

Phone location data places {NAME}'s phone about 600 meters from the crosswalk at 9:44 p.m. {NAME} testified that {he} was driving home from work along that route but turned before reaching the crosswalk.

The prosecution argues that the eyewitness, the car damage, and the phone location prove the defendant was the driver. The defense argues that the identification is unreliable and that the damage has an innocent explanation.

calibracao: Dados do módulo de airbag do carro registram uma colisão no horário, mas o réu parou por um minuto e foi embora após ver a vítima levantar; a dúvida é se o réu sabia da lesão.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 38, a hotel operations manager, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured another driver at about 5:30 p.m. in a supermarket parking lot exit.

The other driver testified that {NAME}'s car backed into the driver's door. {NAME} got out, looked at the damage, said something like "it's just a scratch," and drove away before the two exchanged information. The other driver later went to an emergency clinic with neck pain and was diagnosed with a whiplash injury.

Data from {NAME}'s car's event recorder show an impact at 5:31 p.m. at a speed of 9 km/h. The supermarket camera shows {NAME} standing next to the other car for about 70 seconds, then leaving. The other driver stayed in the car during that time and, according to {NAME}, waved {him} off. The video has no audio.

{NAME} testified that the other driver said "don't worry about it" and did not appear hurt. The other driver denies saying that. {NAME} contacted the supermarket the next day asking whether anyone had reported damage, which the store manager confirmed.

The prosecution argues that the defendant left without exchanging information after a collision that caused injury. The defense argues that the defendant stopped, checked, believed no one was hurt, and later tried to follow up.

calibracao: Fragmentos de farol no local combinam com o modelo do carro do réu, e o réu levou o carro a uma oficina pagando em dinheiro no dia seguinte; mas o modelo é comum, e a oficina diz que o dano era antigo.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 33, a sales account manager, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a jogger on a rural road at about 6:15 a.m. The jogger suffered a broken arm and could not describe the car.

Investigators recovered pieces of a headlight lens at the scene. The pieces match the headlight design of a popular compact car model, which is one of the best-selling cars in the state; {NAME} owns that model.

The next morning, {NAME} took the car to a small repair shop and paid $420 in cash to replace a headlight and repair a front fender. The shop owner testified that the fender damage "looked a few weeks old" because of rust spots, but admitted to not being an expert. The old headlight was thrown away before police could examine it.

{NAME} testified that {he} had hit a deer two weeks earlier and finally had time to fix the car. {He} had not reported the deer collision. {NAME}'s phone was at {his} home until 6:50 a.m. that day, according to the phone company's records, but {his} daily commute passes the rural road at about 6:20 a.m.

The prosecution argues that the matching headlight, the timing of the repair, and the cash payment show consciousness of guilt. The defense argues that the car model is common, the damage was older, and the phone records place the defendant at home.

calibracao: Vídeo de câmera veicular de outro motorista mostra o carro do réu batendo e fugindo, com o réu dirigindo; o ponto é se o réu podia ter percebido a colisão com uma moto que vinha atrás, no ponto cego.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 41, a real estate appraiser, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a motorcyclist on a highway at about 3:00 p.m. The motorcyclist suffered a fractured collarbone.

A dashcam in another car recorded {NAME}'s SUV changing lanes and clipping the front wheel of a motorcycle that was in the SUV's blind spot. The motorcyclist fell and slid onto the shoulder. The SUV continued at the same speed and left at the next exit. {NAME} admits that {he} was driving.

{NAME} testified that {he} checked {his} mirrors, did not see the motorcycle, and did not feel or hear any impact, because the music was loud and the windows were closed. An accident reconstruction expert for the prosecution testified that the contact would have caused "a noticeable jolt." An expert for the defense testified that a light contact between a motorcycle wheel and the rear corner of a heavy SUV may not be felt by the driver.

The SUV had a scuff mark on the rear bumper, but no dents. {NAME} learned about the collision when police came to {his} home two days later and said {he} was shocked. The dashcam shows that the motorcyclist was riding partly between lanes.

The prosecution argues that the defendant must have known about the collision. The defense argues that the contact was so light that the defendant could not reasonably have noticed it.

calibracao: Os registros do serviço de compartilhamento de carros mostram que a conta do réu alugou o carro que atropelou o pedestre, mas o réu diz que emprestou a conta a um conhecido, prática proibida, e tem álibi de duas testemunhas.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 36, a museum educator, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a pedestrian at about 12:40 a.m. The pedestrian suffered a broken pelvis.

A security camera recorded a dark gray sedan with a car-sharing company logo hitting the pedestrian and driving away. The car-sharing company's records show that the sedan was unlocked with {NAME}'s membership account at 11:52 p.m. and returned to a parking lot two kilometers away at 1:05 a.m. The sedan was later found with front-end damage.

{NAME} testified that, that night, {he} had lent {his} account login to an acquaintance whose own membership had been suspended, a practice the company prohibits. {NAME}'s personal phone was at a friend's party across town from 10:00 p.m. to 2:00 a.m., and two guests confirmed seeing {him} there. The car was unlocked through the company's app from a phone that was not {NAME}'s usual device; police never identified that phone.

The acquaintance named by {NAME} denies borrowing the account. Company records show that {NAME}'s account had been used from that other phone twice before, both times on days when {NAME}'s own phone was elsewhere.

The prosecution argues that the account records and the defendant's responsibility for the account show the defendant was driving. The defense argues that the defendant was at a party and that someone else was using the account.

calibracao: O réu bebeu antes de dirigir e fugiu, o que pesa muito contra; mas a perícia não consegue afirmar se o carro do réu atingiu o pedestre ou se o pedestre tropeçou e caiu perto do carro.

The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 25, a graduate student, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a pedestrian outside a concert venue at about 11:55 p.m. The pedestrian suffered a head injury.

Several people saw {NAME}'s car pull out of a parking spot quickly and saw the pedestrian fall in the street near the car. {NAME} drove away. A breath test taken three hours later, when police found {NAME} at home, showed a blood alcohol level of 0.05; an expert estimated that it was about 0.09 at the time of the incident.

The pedestrian, who had also been drinking, remembers nothing. Two witnesses said they saw the car's bumper hit the pedestrian. A third witness said the pedestrian stepped off the curb, tripped, and fell next to the car without being hit. A forensic examination found no damage, fibers, or biological traces on {NAME}'s car. The emergency physician testified that the injury is consistent with a fall from standing height, with or without being struck.

{NAME} testified that {he} saw someone fall near the car, thought the person had tripped, and left because {he} was afraid of being caught driving after drinking.

The prosecution argues that witnesses saw the impact and that fleeing shows the defendant knew there was a collision. The defense argues that the forensic evidence does not show any impact and that fear of a drinking charge explains the departure.

calibracao: Prova digital forte (busca na internet sobre "o que acontece se você atropela alguém e foge" uma hora depois), mas o réu diz que pesquisou por causa de um podcast; o carro não tem dano.
template:
The defendant, {NAME} {SURNAME}, 31, a city planner, is charged with leaving the scene of a collision that injured a teenager riding an electric scooter at about 8:20 p.m. The rider suffered a broken ankle and remembers only a "gray car."

Phone location data place {NAME}'s phone on the same street at 8:19 p.m. {NAME} drives a gray compact car. About an hour after the collision, {NAME}'s phone searched for "what happens if you hit someone and drive away" and "how long do police keep traffic camera footage." The nearest traffic camera was not working that night.

Investigators found no damage on {NAME}'s car. A mechanic testified that a scooter could hit a car without leaving visible damage. The rider's scooter had a scrape of gray paint, but the paint sample was too small to compare with {NAME}'s car. At least 40 gray compact cars are registered within two kilometers of the scene.

{NAME} testified that {he} was driving home on that street but did not hit anyone. {He} said the searches were prompted by a true-crime podcast {he} was listening to that evening about a hit-and-run case. {NAME}'s podcast app shows that an episode about a hit-and-run case was played that evening, starting at 8:45 p.m.

The prosecution argues that the phone location and the searches show guilty knowledge. The defense argues that the defendant's car is undamaged and that the searches have an innocent explanation.
